messages:
alice: Hey — hitting a nasty combo of pnpm hoisting + package exports that breaks our JS SDK in edge runtimes (Vercel Edge / Cloudflare). error: "Package subpath './dist/index.cjs' is not defined by 'exports'" when importing from a consumer monorepo.

ben: Oof. Can you paste the package.json exports and a minimal monorepo layout?

alice: Sure. layout:
- /repo/packages/sdk/package.json
- /repo/apps/web/package.json (depends on sdk)

sdk package.json exports snippet:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
},
"main": "dist/index.cjs",
"module": "dist/index.mjs",
"types": "dist/index.d.ts",
"type": "module"
```
consumer does `import { createClient } from 'redwood-sdk'` in an edge function and bundler fails with that subpath error. Node dev server works fine locally.

carla: Two things I've seen: (1) pnpm creates nested node_modules symlink layout, some bundlers/edge resolvers don't follow the symlink to the package root so they end up resolving the package.json from a different path and then the exports mapping doesn’t match. (2) If your monorepo tooling is building the SDK into packages/sdk/dist and then hoisting a different copy, consumers might pick up an incomplete package (no dist files) at runtime.

dave: For (1) a pragmatic workaround is to add an explicit fallback export that matches the path the bundler is trying to read, e.g. add "./dist/index.cjs": "./dist/index.cjs" or "./dist/*": "./dist/*" to exports. Ugly but often fixes packers that directly import a file path. Also ensure "./package.json": "./package.json" is present (you already have that).

ben: Another lever: pnpm config — if you set `node-linker=hoisted` or run `pnpm install --shamefully-hoist` in CI for the app, it makes resolution closer to classic npm/yarn hoisting and many bundlers behave. Downsides: you lose some space/speed benefits and can hide connector bugs. But good short-term mitigation for customers using edge platforms that choke on symlinks.

carla: For TS consumers: if types disappear due to hoisting, add `typesVersions` in package.json or export a "types" subpath: "exports": {"./types": "./dist/index.d.ts", ... } so TS resolves fiber directly. Otherwise tsc/node resolve can miss the hoisted d.ts location.

alice: Helpful. One more weirdness: when the SDK's package.json has "type":"module" consumers that `require('redwood-sdk')` in some serverless shards get a syntax error. Is the canonical fix to ship a tiny cjs bridge at `dist/index.cjs` that does `module.exports = require('./index.mjs').default`?

dave: Yes — publish both build artifacts and conditionally export them. Example exports to support ESM/CJS consumers + bundlers:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs" },
  "./dist/index.cjs": "./dist/index.cjs",
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
Make sure the cjs file uses CommonJS (not `import`/`export`) and points at compiled code. That pattern covers Node, bundlers, and edge runtimes that try to read file subpaths.

ben: For monorepo dev DX also consider adding an app-level preinstall script that verifies built artifacts exist for local testing: `pnpm -w -r --filter sdk build`. Or on publish we can enforce `files` in package.json so partial copies don't get hoisted without the dist folder.

carla: FYI Yarn Berry has different behaviors — if you support both, recommend documenting the `pnpm` and `yarn` quirks in the SDK README (short checklist: build before local consumption, export cjs bridge, add ./package.json export, optional shamefully-hoist tip). Saves support tickets.

ci-bot: created issue #3812: "sdk: edge import failures with pnpm hoisting and exports mapping" (assign: @alice) :robot_face:

alice: Great — I'll: 1) add explicit dist subpath exports + cjs bridge, 2) add types subpath, 3) add a short troubleshooting blurb in README about pnpm hoisting/shamefully-hoist and yarn nohoist. Will drop a PR and request reviews. Thanks all :raised_hands:
